title: Print Hello, World!
instruction: Write a `print()` statement that outputs **Hello, World!** exactly as shown.
test_suite:
import io, sys

def test_prints_hello_world():
    captured = io.StringIO()
    sys.stdout = captured
    exec(open("exercise.py").read())
    sys.stdout = sys.__stdout__
    output = captured.getvalue()
    assert output == 'Hello, World!\n', f"Expected Hello, World!, got {output!r}"

import io, sys, re

def test_prints_two_lines():
    captured = io.StringIO()
    sys.stdout = captured
    exec(open("exercise.py").read())
    sys.stdout = sys.__stdout__
    output = captured.getvalue()
    assert re.match('.+\n.+\n*', output), f"Output should have two lines, got {output!r}"

title: Print your favorite color
instruction: Print your **favorite color**: Red, Blue, Green, Yellow, Purple, Orange, Pink, Black.
starter_code: # Pick a color and print it
test_suite:
import io, sys

def test_prints_allowed_color():
    captured = io.StringIO()
    sys.stdout = captured
    exec(open("exercise.py").read())
    sys.stdout = sys.__stdout__
    output = captured.getvalue()
    allowed = ["Red", "Blue", "Green", "Yellow", "Purple", "Orange", "Pink", "Black"]
    assert output.strip() in allowed, f"Output should be a valid color, got {output!r}"
